Solon is one of Roubic's flagship markets — {{global.owner_name}} has worked its streets since 1992. The trees that make Solon look like Solon (heritage oaks, mature maples, EAB-risk ash, and original-growth pines) are the same ones that come down in a high-wind event, and we know which lots have sandstone bedrock that limits access and which need mat protection.

Permits, Insurance & the Solon Storm Corridor

Solon sits in NE Ohio's high-wind and derecho exposure corridor, so a mature canopy plus recurring storm events means tree-on-structure work every year. When a removal requires a city permit, Roubic assesses the DBH before quoting and pulls the Solon permit on your behalf — the filing fee is billed at cost with no markup, and hazardous trees are exempt with arborist documentation.

Certificates of insurance are already on file with Solon-area HOAs and the city itself, so emergency work doesn't wait on a fresh insurance review. Carriers generally reimburse only when a tree damages a covered structure, so our documentation package is built to clear the carrier on the first submission.

Common Solon Storm Questions

Solon Storm & Emergency FAQ

Six things Solon homeowners and property managers ask before a storm hits.

How fast does Roubic respond to tree emergencies in Solon?
Our target on-site window for active Solon emergencies is 2–4 hours from the Auburn Township yard, 7 miles away. Active emergencies are tree-on-structure, driveway-blocking, or leaning hazard trees that could fail before scheduled service. The 24/7 emergency line is {{global.phone}}, dispatched directly from the yard.
What does Roubic do for Solon insurance claims on storm-damaged trees?
We provide the full documentation package your carrier needs: scene photos, itemized scope, species and DBH estimates, before/after photos, and a written summary matched to the carrier's loss notice. Insurance typically covers tree removal only when a tree damages a covered structure — a house, garage, fence, or vehicle — not routine standing-tree removal.
Will Roubic dispatch to Solon during an active high-wind event?
Crew safety governs deployment. We do not send climbers or crane operators into active high winds or lightning. Once conditions are safe — typically within 2–4 hours of the storm passing — we deploy aggressively, staging multiple jobs in priority order. For before-the-storm planning, see our Storm Preparation Checklist.
Does Roubic do after-hours work for Solon property-management firms?
Yes. Several Solon-area landscape and property-management companies use Roubic as their after-hours emergency tree subcontractor — including a documented response to a multi-tree storm event for a regional landscaping firm in 2024. Certificates of insurance are already on file with area HOAs and the city.
What if a tree falls on my house in Solon after-hours?
Call {{global.phone}} immediately. We dispatch a crew with crane support for tree-on-structure extraction, photograph the scene for insurance documentation, tarp the roof opening if needed, and coordinate next-day full extraction and cleanup. Don't enter the damaged area until the crew arrives — branch shifts can be unpredictable.
How much does storm and emergency tree work cost in Solon?
Final price depends on access, height, structure proximity, and equipment. Honest brackets from real jobs: small tree under 30 ft $300–$700; medium 30–60 ft $700–$1,800; large heritage oak 60–80 ft $1,800–$3,500; crane-assist 80 ft+ $3,500–$7,000+. After-hours emergency dispatch adds roughly a 30% premium, and most insurance-coverable jobs land between $1,200 and $8,000. Every estimate is free and quoted on-site.
